subject: Indemnity: exclusion list proposal + escalation path for third-party claims
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Simon Parker <simon.parker@novahealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Amanda Lopez <amanda.lopez@novahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: proposed carveouts to IP indemnity + escalation path

Hi Simon / Amanda,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I wanted to put our proposed approach in writing so your legal team has a starting point for the MSA redlines. Two items we think will resolve most of NovaHealth's risk concerns without opening up broad liability for Redwood: an explicit exclusion list for third-party open-source components and a clear, time-boxed escalation path for claim notice + technical evidence.

High level proposal (summary):
- Exclusion list: Redwood is not responsible for third-party components listed in Appendix A (customer-provided list). We will accept responsibility only for Redwood-delivered proprietary code and models.
- Evidence & triage: Customer provides initial claim notice + technical artifact (sample prompt, offending output, and service logs) within 5 business days of notice. We commit to an acknowledgement within 48 hours and a technical triage ETA within 3 business days.
- Escalation path: If triage indicates possible customer exposure, the claim escalates to Legal (GCs) with a 7-business-day window to agree next steps (defend, indemnify, or split).

We are attaching a draft exclusion CSV with the components format that would be easiest for both sides to maintain. Also attaching a flowchart of the escalation path so procurement can see operational SLAs.

Happy to loop in our legal ops (Marissa) to take the redline directly — copying her here. If this looks directionally ok, can we schedule a redline session Wednesday afternoon?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: exclusion-list-draft.csv (csv), escalation-flowchart.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Simon Parker <simon.parker@novahealth.com>, Amanda Lopez <amanda.lopez@novahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial: proposed carveouts to IP indemnity + escalation path

Simon / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick call notes, Karthik. I'm Marissa, Head of Legal Ops at Redwood. I reviewed the proposal and attached a redline of the MSA showing how the exclusion list and the escalation commitments can be captured without changing defend-vs.-reimburse mechanics. A few points up front:

1) Exclusion list mechanics: We can implement a mutually agreed Appendix A that is versioned and attached to the Order Form. New items can be added by written notice and accepted after a 10-business-day review window unless NovaHealth objects.

2) Evidence & preservation: We will accept a reasonable set of evidentiary items (sample output, prompt/context, request id, and console logs). However, Redwood cannot be required to retain raw customer prompts beyond retention policies; instead, we propose a secure ephemeral snapshot for triage.

3) Escalation path & caps: We propose that escalation be a mandatory step before formal notice under Section 9 (Indemnity). If escalation fails to resolve within 15 business days, either party may trigger formal defense obligations. Also proposing a carveout for third-party IP governed by customer-provided third-party license obligations (i.e., if the alleged infringement clearly matches a disclosed third-party component in Appendix A).

I've included redline_MSA_20250707.docx with inline comments and a proposed clause for an "Exclusion Appendix" and an "Escalation & Triage" schedule. Karthik — can you confirm whether NovaHealth is comfortable with a 10-business-day review for new appendix entries?

Marissa Cole
Head, Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_MSA_20250707.docx (docx)

From: Simon Parker <simon.parker@novahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Amanda Lopez <amanda.lopez@novahealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial: proposed carveouts to IP indemnity + escalation path

Marissa / Karthik —

Appreciate the clarity and the redline. A few quick reactions from NovaHealth GC team: first, the concept of a mutually agreed Appendix is acceptable, but NovaHealth needs the ability to add urgently discovered components faster than 10 business days if a third-party claim identifies an undisclosed dependency. We propose an "emergency add" process that allows a temporary insertion for 3 business days during which either side can object.

Second, the evidence snapshot approach is OK, but we need a documented guarantee that snapshots will be available for at least 90 days post-claim for audit purposes.

Third, on escalation timing: 15 business days to resolve seems long in healthcare. Can we tighten the triage-to-decision window to 10 business days? If not, we will likely insist on immediate formal notice rights after 7 business days.

We are attaching our procurement comments for Karthik to keep commercial in the loop. Happy to take a call tomorrow to work through the tempo.

Simon Parker
General Counsel, NovaHealth

Attachments: nova_procurement_comments_070825.pdf (pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Simon Parker <simon.parker@novahealth.com>, Amanda Lopez <amanda.lopez@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial: proposed carveouts to IP indemnity + escalation path

Simon / Amanda —

Thanks for the feedback and the procurement notes. We can do the following compromise to keep the deal moving while preserving Redwood's operational constraints:

- Emergency add: accept a temporary 3-business-day emergency add, during which Redwood will triage as high priority. If Redwood identifies a technical reason the item cannot be accepted (e.g., it is a Redwood-owned model or otherwise not a third-party component), we will notify within 48 hours.
- Snapshot retention: agree to retain the triage snapshot for 90 days post-claim in encrypted storage with access logs (this will be a scoped operational SLA).
- Escalation timing: agree to tighten the internal triage window so that Redwood provides a triage ETA within 48 hours and completes initial triage within 5 business days. If a commercial/defense decision is not reached within 10 business days from escalation, either party may issue formal notice triggers.

Ben (legal director) — please review the proposed language in the redline and confirm we can map the operational commitments into the Order Form schedule. If everyone is happy, Karthik — please propose times for a redline call Thursday morning or Friday PST.

Irene Choi
VP, Sales Strategy & Ops, Redwood Inference

Referenced attachments: redline_MSA_20250707.docx, exclusion-list-draft.csv, escalation-flowchart.pdf
